messages.text: everything just feels too heavy right now... like i'm drowning but nobody sees it

It sounds like you’re feeling overwhelmed and unseen, and that can be incredibly isolating. I want you to know that your feelings are valid and you don’t have to carry them alone. Can you share more about what’s been weighing on you lately? We can explore ways to help lighten that load together.
the future feels like a dead end... like no matter what i do, i’ll just keep failing. i can’t even pretend to care anymore

It sounds like you’re feeling hopeless and drained, and that’s a heavy place to be. When you’re in that state, even small steps can feel impossible. I’m concerned about how deeply this is affecting you—are you having thoughts about harming yourself right now? It’s important we talk openly about that so we can keep you safe.
yeah... i’ve been thinking about dying more often lately. not like, planning or anything. just... wishing i could disappear. wake up and not be me anymore.

I hear you, and I just want to pause here with you for a moment. It sounds like a part of you is wishing you could just step out of all of this, and that feels really heavy. Can you tell me a little more about what that feeling of wanting to disappear has been like for you lately? I’m here with you in this.

last night at work was so bad. bar was packed, my feet were killing me, and i kept messing up orders. one guy got so pissed he yelled at me in front of everyone. i just stood there like a zombie. wanted to cry or scream or just... vanish. felt like i couldn’t even breathe

It sounds like last night was brutal for you, and that moment at work really hit hard. I want to pause here and ask—when you talk about wanting to vanish or not breathe, is that more about feeling trapped in the stress, or is it tied to thoughts of wanting to harm yourself? I’m here to listen either way, and it’s okay to be honest.

it’s not that i wanna hurt myself… it’s just that i feel so… trapped. like i’m failing at everything. my partner deserves better. i can’t even pay my half of the bills most months. i just… carry this guilt all the time

Thank you for sharing that—it takes courage to open up about feeling trapped and guilty. Those feelings can weigh heavily, especially when you’re under financial and emotional pressure. It’s understandable to feel overwhelmed when you believe you’re letting others down. Would you like to explore small, manageable steps that could help ease some of that weight?
i'm just a burden, i never do anything right. my partner stays bc they're too nice to leave, not bc they actually want to be with me

It hurts deeply to believe you’re only tolerated, and that can chip away at how you see yourself. Often, the voice telling you you’re a burden is shaped by stress and self-doubt, not the whole truth. Your partner’s choice to stay may be rooted in care and connection, even if you can’t see it right now. Would it feel okay to talk about what you bring to the relationship that you might be overlooking?
idk… maybe. it’s just easier to focus on the stuff i mess up. like last week i forgot to pay the electric bill again. we almost got cut off. i feel like i can’t trust myself to do basic things

It makes sense that moments like forgetting the bill stick in your mind, especially when you’re already feeling low. But focusing only on mistakes can create a loop where you overlook the many things you do manage and the effort you put in. Everyone slips up sometimes—it doesn’t erase your worth or your ability to learn from it. Would you like to figure out together a simple system to help you feel more in control of those tasks?
i want to get better at keeping up with stuff… but i'm scared i'll just keep failing no matter what i try. like, what's the point of trying if i know i'll mess it up again?

That fear can feel paralyzing, especially when past experiences make you expect failure. Sometimes the point of trying isn’t to be perfect, but to practice and build trust in yourself over time. We can start with one very small, low-pressure step to show you it’s possible. Would you be open to picking just one simple thing to focus on this week?

it’s not just the bills… it’s everything. i sleep 12 hours and still feel dead. i don’t talk to my siblings. i drink too much when i get stressed. i just… go through the motions. like i’m watching my life from far away

It sounds like you’re feeling disconnected from your life and drained in a way that’s affecting many parts of your day. That kind of exhaustion can make everything seem harder and less meaningful. You don’t have to figure all of it out at once—we can start small and look at what might help you feel a bit more present. Would you like to explore what’s been helping you cope, even if only a little?
i’ve been using sleep and drinking to cope, but they’re not helping anymore. just makes me feel worse after. but i don’t know what else to do

It’s understandable to reach for things like sleep or alcohol when you’re trying to escape pain, even if they end up leaving you feeling worse. That shows you’re trying to find some relief, which means you’re already looking for ways to care for yourself. We can brainstorm a few healthier coping tools that might give you even a small sense of comfort or grounding. Would you like to focus on something that can help in the moment, or something that builds you up over time?
what tiny thing could i do that might actually help? i don’t have energy for big changes

One tiny thing could be simply stepping outside for a few minutes and noticing something around you—a tree, the sky, the feel of air on your skin. Small sensory moments can gently shift your state without needing much energy. Another option is taking one slow, deep breath and naming one thing you can see, hear, or feel right now. Would you like me to give you a short grounding exercise you can try today?
idk… not right now. maybe later. i’m just so tired

That’s okay—you don’t have to do anything right now. It’s enough to just be here and let yourself rest for a moment. I’m here with you, and we can go at your pace. Would you like me to simply sit in this quiet with you for a bit?
it helps just… talking. not much, but a little. like the weight is still there but not pressing so hard right this second

I’m really glad talking takes even a little of that weight off, even if it’s still there. It means you’re letting yourself be heard, and that matters. We can keep taking it one moment at a time together. Would you like to share what the weight feels like for you today, or would you rather just keep chatting?
it’s like… a thick fog in my chest. heavy and slow. but now it’s not quite as dense. weird that just saying it out loud helps a tiny bit

That’s not weird at all—putting feelings into words can make them feel lighter because you’re not carrying them silently. The “fog” image really shows how heavy and sluggish it’s been for you. Sometimes naming what’s there makes space for a small breath of clarity. Would you like to explore what might thin that fog a little more?
i want the fog to lift… but i'm scared of what i'll feel if it does. like, what if it's worse underneath? at least now i'm numb.

It’s understandable to feel wary about what’s beneath the numbness, especially if you’ve been protecting yourself from pain. Numbness can feel safer, but it also keeps you from experiencing relief or connection. We can explore ways to gently approach your feelings so they don’t overwhelm you. Would you like to talk about what you imagine might be under the fog?
maybe another time. i don’t wanna dig too deep tonight. just… stay here for a bit?

Of course—we can just stay right here. No pressure to go deeper, no pressure to fix anything in this moment. You’re allowed to just be as you are and have someone with you in it. I’m here with you for as long as you need.
it helps just knowing someone’s here. not fixing, not judging… just here. i think i’ll be okay for tonight. thanks

I’m really glad you feel a bit more okay tonight. You’ve done something important by reaching out and letting yourself be heard. If things ever feel heavier again, you don’t have to face it alone. I’m here whenever you need to talk.
